dialogue.text: Good morning, Doctor. I've noticed a sudden sensitivity in one of my molars. It becomes particularly uncomfortable whenever I bite down on something hard or have a cold drink.

dialogue.speaker: Doctor
dialogue.text: Does anything in particular bring on the discomfort?

dialogue.speaker: Patient
dialogue.text: Yes. Cold drinks seem to bring it on, and sometimes I get a brief, throbbing sensation when I bite on that tooth.

dialogue.speaker: Doctor
dialogue.text: Have you noticed any swelling or tenderness around the tooth?

dialogue.speaker: Patient
dialogue.text: There's no noticeable swelling, but the area around the tooth feels slightly tender when I press on it.

dialogue.speaker: Doctor
dialogue.text: All right. Let me take a closer look. I'll check the tooth for any visible signs of decay and see how it reacts to pressure and temperature.

dialogue.speaker: Patient
dialogue.text: Okay, Doctor.

dialogue.speaker: Doctor
dialogue.text: I can see a small cavity on the surface of your molar. There's also some discoloration around the affected area.

dialogue.speaker: Patient
dialogue.text: Does that mean I have dental caries?

dialogue.speaker: Doctor
dialogue.text: Yes, it appears that you have an early stage of dental caries. The decay hasn't reached the deeper layers of the tooth yet, which is a positive sign.

dialogue.speaker: Patient
dialogue.text: What might have caused it?

dialogue.speaker: Doctor
dialogue.text: Several factors could be involved. Frequent exposure to sugary foods, inadequate brushing, and a lack of fluoride can all contribute to tooth decay.

dialogue.speaker: Patient
dialogue.text: I've been having sweet snacks quite often recently. Could that be making the problem worse?

dialogue.speaker: Doctor
dialogue.text: It could. When you frequently consume sugary foods, bacteria in your mouth produce acids that gradually weaken the enamel.

dialogue.speaker: Patient
dialogue.text: So, what kind of treatment would I need?

dialogue.speaker: Doctor
dialogue.text: At this stage, a filling should be enough. I'll remove the decayed part of the tooth. If you feel any pain during the procedure, I'll give you a local anaesthetic injection to make you more comfortable.

dialogue.speaker: Patient
dialogue.text: I understand. And what can I do to prevent another cavity?

dialogue.speaker: Doctor
dialogue.text: Brush your teeth twice a day with fluoride toothpaste, clean between your teeth regularly, and try to limit sugary snacks between meals.

dialogue.speaker: Patient
dialogue.text: Would regular dental check-ups help as well?

dialogue.speaker: Doctor
dialogue.text: Absolutely. If cavities are detected early, they can usually be treated before they cause more serious damage.

dialogue.speaker: Patient
dialogue.text: That makes sense. I'll pay more attention to my oral hygiene from now on.

dialogue.speaker: Doctor
dialogue.text: Good. We can treat the cavity with a filling before the decay gets any deeper.

dialogue.speaker: Patient
dialogue.text: All right, Doctor. I'm ready to have it treated.

dialogue.speaker: Doctor
dialogue.text: Excellent. We'll get started shortly. Taking care of it now will help protect the tooth from further damage.

dialogue.speaker: Patient
dialogue.text: Thank you, Doctor. I appreciate your explanation.

dialogue.speaker: Doctor
dialogue.text: You're very welcome.

tests.question: What is the medical meaning of the term 'dental caries' in clinical consultation?
tests.explanation: 'dental caries' atamasining to'g'ri ma'nosi: tish kariyesi.

tests.question: Which term corresponds to 'kariyes o'chog'i / kovak'?
tests.explanation: 'kariyes o'chog'i / kovak' ma'nosiga mos keluvchi tibbiy termin 'cavity' hisoblanadi.

tests.question: Which of the following is the grammatically and clinically standard question to ask about the duration of symptoms?
tests.option_a: How long do you having this symptom?
tests.option_b: How long has this condition been bothering you?
tests.option_c: Since what time you have this problem?
tests.option_d: How many days you are feeling pain?
tests.explanation: Klinik anamnezda davomiylikni so'rash uchun Present Perfect Continuous ('How long has... been bothering you?') to'g'ri shakl hisoblanadi.

tests.question: When evaluating acute pain, what is the best phrasing to assess pain character?
tests.option_a: Is your pain bad or very bad?
tests.option_b: Can you describe the pain—is it sharp, dull, throbbing, or aching?
tests.option_c: Why do you have sharp pain today?
tests.explanation: Og'riq xarakterini aniqlashda shifokor ochiq va taklif qiluvchi variantlar (sharp, dull, throbbing, aching) beradi.
